title: What does each child get when 2 rotis are shared among 4 children?
description: Each of the two rotis is cut into four equal pieces and each child takes two pieces, which is two fourths. The two pieces join to make one half, and the division, addition and multiplication facts are written.
teaching_notes: One idea: two rotis shared among four children gives two fourths each, and two fourths is the same as one half. Watch for students who say each child gets two rotis or leave the answer as two fourths without seeing it is a half.

source: Figure it Out Q2 (section 7.6, second block)
video_script.why: A learner finds the share when two rotis are shared equally among four children, draws it, and writes the division, addition and multiplication facts.
video_script.substitution: none: the book's own rotis shared among four children, with a picture
video_script.anchor: two rotis drawn on a table and four children waiting to share them
video_script.payoff_line: Each child gets one half of a roti

final_answer.value: Each child gets 1/2 roti (2/4 = 1/2). Division fact: 2 ÷ 4 = 2/4 = 1/2. Addition fact: 2 = 1/2 + 1/2 + 1/2 + 1/2. Multiplication fact: 2 = 4 × 1/2.
final_answer.spoken: each child gets one half of a roti, with the division, addition and multiplication facts

maths_rules: 2 rotis among 4 children: cut each roti into 4 equal pieces, giving 8 pieces
8 pieces among 4 children is 2 pieces each, so each child gets 2/4
2 pieces of one fourth join to make half a roti, so 2/4 = 1/2
video_script.design: One idea: the share can be written in two ways, as two fourths and as one half. The picture of the two rotis stays on the board and the pieces join.
